about: Plain-English explainers for every metric (the exact metric name, or the LL Strength test id). 'what' is for athletes, patients and coaches (20 words at most) and shows when a metric name is tapped and under each Top priority on the PDF; 'how' is an optional protocol reminder for the clinician, shown on the screen only. Edit the wording here; the app picks it up the next time it opens online.

Jump Height.what: How high you jump from standing after a quick dip: a simple measure of lower-body power.
Jump Height.how: CMJ on ForceDecks, hands on hips; best of 3; jump height by impulse-momentum.

Peak Power.what: The most power your legs produce during the jump, relative to body weight.
Peak Power.how: From the CMJ trials: Peak Power / BM (W/kg).

CMJ Peak Force.what: The highest force you push into the ground while driving up out of the jump.
CMJ Peak Force.how: CMJ concentric peak force (N); also used for DSI.

RSI-modified.what: How quickly you turn a dip into a jump: jump height divided by the time taken to leave the ground.
RSI-modified.how: From the CMJ trials: jump height ÷ time to take-off.

Concentric Asymmetry.what: The difference between your left and right legs while pushing up out of the jump.
Concentric Asymmetry.how: CMJ concentric peak force asymmetry (%); tick the higher side.

Landing Asymmetry.what: The difference between your left and right legs when absorbing the landing.
Landing Asymmetry.how: CMJ landing force asymmetry (%); tick the higher side.

IMTP Peak Force.what: Your maximum whole-body pulling strength against a fixed bar.
IMTP Peak Force.how: Isometric mid-thigh pull on ForceDecks; best of 2–3 maximal pulls of 3–5 s.

IMTP Relative Force.what: Maximum pulling strength relative to body weight, so athletes of different sizes can be compared.
IMTP Relative Force.how: IMTP peak vertical force ÷ body mass (N/kg).

IMTP RFD 0–200 ms.what: How fast you build force in the first fifth of a second of a maximal pull.
IMTP RFD 0–200 ms.how: Rate of force development 0–200 ms from the IMTP trials.

Hop RSI (best).what: How springy you are over quick repeated hops: jump height compared with time on the ground.
Hop RSI (best).how: Repeated hop test (e.g. 10/5) on ForceDecks; best RSI.

Hop Contact Time.what: How long your feet stay on the ground between quick hops. Shorter is better.
Hop Contact Time.how: Ground contact time from the repeated hop test (s).

Hop Jump Height.what: How high you get off the ground during the quick repeated hops.
Hop Jump Height.how: Jump height from the repeated hop test (cm).

Reactive Asymmetry.what: The difference between your left and right legs during the quick repeated hops.
Reactive Asymmetry.how: Repeated hop test asymmetry (%); tick the higher side.

Nordic Peak Force — Left.what: Left hamstring strength while lowering your body forward under control in a Nordic curl.
Nordic Peak Force — Left.how: NordBord; slow Nordic lowers; best peak force, left leg.

Nordic Peak Force — Right.what: Right hamstring strength while lowering your body forward under control in a Nordic curl.
Nordic Peak Force — Right.how: NordBord; slow Nordic lowers; best peak force, right leg.

Nordic L/R Imbalance.what: The difference in hamstring strength between your legs on the Nordic test.
Nordic L/R Imbalance.how: NordBord imbalance (%); tick the stronger side.

Nordic Relative Force.what: Nordic hamstring strength relative to body weight.

Adductor Peak Force.what: How strongly you squeeze your knees together: inner-thigh (groin) strength.
Adductor Peak Force.how: ForceFrame adduction squeeze in the clinic's standard position; best rep.

Abductor Peak Force.what: How strongly you push your knees apart: outer-hip strength.
Abductor Peak Force.how: ForceFrame abduction, same position as the adductor test; best rep.

Adduction Asymmetry.what: The difference in groin squeeze strength between your left and right sides.
Adduction Asymmetry.how: ForceFrame adduction asymmetry (%); tick the stronger side.

Add : Abd Ratio.what: The balance between groin and outer-hip strength (inner ÷ outer).
Add : Abd Ratio.how: Adductor ÷ abductor peak force from the same ForceFrame session.

DSI (CMJ ÷ IMTP).what: Jump force compared with maximum strength, which helps show whether strength or explosiveness needs more work.
DSI (CMJ ÷ IMTP).how: Worked out by the app: CMJ peak force ÷ IMTP peak force.

Isometric Peak Force.what: The most force produced in a held (static) strength test on the DynaMo.
Isometric Peak Force.how: DynaMo isometric test; note the muscle group and position in Notes.

Quad ISO @ 60° — Left.what: Left thigh (quadriceps) strength pushing the knee straight, with the knee bent to 60 degrees.
Quad ISO @ 60° — Left.how: DynaMo isometric knee extension at 60° flexion; enter force in N.

Quad ISO @ 60° — Right.what: Right thigh (quadriceps) strength pushing the knee straight, with the knee bent to 60 degrees.
Quad ISO @ 60° — Right.how: DynaMo isometric knee extension at 60° flexion; enter force in N.

10 m sprint.what: Time to sprint 10 metres from a standing start: acceleration. Shorter is better.
10 m sprint.how: SmartSpeed gates; standing start; best of 2–3.

20 m sprint.what: Time to sprint 20 metres: acceleration building towards top speed. Shorter is better.
20 m sprint.how: SmartSpeed gates; same start as the 10 m; best of 2–3.

30 m sprint.what: Time to sprint 30 metres: acceleration and speed. Shorter is better.

5-10-5 (pro-agility).what: Change-of-direction speed: sprint 5 metres, turn, 10 metres, turn, then 5 metres.
5-10-5 (pro-agility).how: Pro-agility shuttle timed with SmartSpeed; best of 2.

AKET deficit vs uninjured.what: How much less the injured leg's knee straightens than the other leg's, with the hip bent. Smaller is better.
AKET deficit vs uninjured.how: Active knee extension test, hip at 90°; degrees short of the uninjured side.

PKET deficit vs uninjured.what: Hamstring flexibility gap when the knee is straightened for you, compared with the other leg. Smaller is better.
PKET deficit vs uninjured.how: Passive knee extension test, hip at 90°; degrees short of the uninjured side.

SLR % of uninjured side.what: How high the injured leg lifts while kept straight, as a percentage of the other leg.
SLR % of uninjured side.how: Passive straight-leg raise; injured ÷ uninjured angle × 100.

MHFAKE % of uninjured side.what: Hamstring flexibility with the hip fully bent, as a percentage of the other leg.
MHFAKE % of uninjured side.how: Maximal hip flexion active knee extension; injured ÷ uninjured × 100.

HHD 90° knee-flex force — injured.what: Injured-leg hamstring strength pulling the heel down, with the knee bent to 90 degrees.
HHD 90° knee-flex force — injured.how: Hand-held dynamometer, knee at 90° flexion; best of 3 (N).

HHD 90° knee-flex % of uninjured.what: Injured-leg hamstring strength at 90 degrees of knee bend, as a percentage of the other leg.
HHD 90° knee-flex % of uninjured.how: HHD at 90° knee flexion; injured ÷ uninjured × 100.

HHD 15° knee-flex force — injured.what: Injured-leg hamstring strength with the knee almost straight (15 degrees of bend).
HHD 15° knee-flex force — injured.how: Hand-held dynamometer, knee at 15° flexion; best of 3 (N).

HHD 45° force — injured.what: Injured-leg hamstring strength with the knee bent to 45 degrees.
HHD 45° force — injured.how: Hand-held dynamometer, knee at 45° flexion; best of 3 (N).

Nordic peak force — injured.what: Injured-leg hamstring strength while lowering your body forward under control in a Nordic curl.
Nordic peak force — injured.how: NordBord; slow Nordic lowers; best peak force, injured side.

Nordic peak-force imbalance.what: The difference in Nordic hamstring strength between your legs, in newtons. Smaller is better.
Nordic peak-force imbalance.how: NordBord left–right difference in peak force (N).

Knee-flexor ECC peak torque @60°/s — inj.what: Injured-leg hamstring strength while the muscle lengthens under load on an isokinetic machine.
Knee-flexor ECC peak torque @60°/s — inj.how: Isokinetic eccentric knee flexion at 60°/s; peak torque (Nm).

Knee-flexor CONC peak torque @60°/s diff.what: How much weaker the injured hamstring is than the other leg when bending the knee. Smaller is better.
Knee-flexor CONC peak torque @60°/s diff.how: Isokinetic concentric knee flexion at 60°/s; % difference between sides.

5 m sprint time.what: Time to sprint 5 metres: first-step acceleration. Shorter is better.
5 m sprint time.how: SmartSpeed gates; standing start; best of 2–3.

10 m sprint time.what: Time to sprint 10 metres: acceleration. Shorter is better.
10 m sprint time.how: SmartSpeed gates; standing start; best of 2–3.

HaOS score.what: A questionnaire score (0–100) of how the hamstring feels and works in daily life and sport.
HaOS score.how: Hamstring Outcome Score, completed by the patient.

Pain on palpation — length.what: Length of the tender area along the hamstring when it is pressed. Smaller is better.
Pain on palpation — length.how: Palpate along the muscle; measure the tender length (cm).

IKDC.what: A questionnaire score (0–100) of knee symptoms, function and sport. Higher is better.
IKDC.how: IKDC Subjective Knee Form, completed by the patient.

KOOS — ADL.what: Questionnaire score (0–100) for how easily you manage daily activities with your knee.
KOOS — ADL.how: KOOS Activities of Daily Living subscale.

KOOS — Pain.what: Questionnaire score (0–100) for knee pain; a higher score means less pain.

KOOS — QOL.what: Questionnaire score (0–100) for how much your knee affects your quality of life.

KOOS — Sport & Rec.what: Questionnaire score (0–100) for sport and recreation tasks such as running, jumping and twisting.

KOOS — Symptoms.what: Questionnaire score (0–100) for knee swelling, stiffness and other symptoms; higher means fewer symptoms.

ACL-RSI.what: A questionnaire score (0–100) of confidence and emotional readiness to return to sport.
ACL-RSI.how: ACL Return to Sport after Injury scale, completed by the patient.

Cincinnati Knee Score.what: A knee questionnaire score (0–100) covering symptoms and function in daily life and sport.

GRS Perceived Function.what: How normal your knee feels overall, rated from 0 to 100.
GRS Perceived Function.how: Global Rating Scale of perceived function (100 = pre-injury level).

Pedi-IKDC.what: The children's version of the IKDC knee questionnaire (0–100).

Knee extension torque — injured.what: Thigh (quadriceps) strength of the operated leg, straightening the knee on a strength machine.
Knee extension torque — injured.how: Isokinetic or isometric knee extension; peak torque (Nm), injured side.

Knee flexion torque — injured.what: Hamstring strength of the operated leg, bending the knee on a strength machine.
Knee flexion torque — injured.how: Isokinetic or isometric knee flexion; peak torque (Nm), injured side.

Knee extension LSI.what: Operated-leg thigh (quadriceps) strength as a percentage of the other leg.

Knee flexion LSI.what: Operated-leg hamstring strength as a percentage of the other leg.

Quadriceps LSI.what: Operated-leg thigh (quadriceps) strength as a percentage of the other leg.
Quadriceps LSI.how: Enter left and right from the same test; the app works out injured ÷ other side × 100.

Hamstring LSI.what: Operated-leg hamstring strength as a percentage of the other leg.
Hamstring LSI.how: Injured ÷ uninjured hamstring force or torque × 100.

Quadriceps strength index (90° ISO).what: Operated-leg thigh strength with the knee bent to 90 degrees, as a percentage of the other leg.
Quadriceps strength index (90° ISO).how: Isometric knee extension at 90°; injured ÷ uninjured × 100.

CMJ — Jump height.what: How high you jump from standing on both legs after a quick dip.
CMJ — Jump height.how: CMJ on ForceDecks, hands on hips; best of 3.

CMJ — Peak power.what: The most power produced during the jump, relative to body weight.

CMJ — Concentric impulse.what: The total push into the ground while driving up out of the jump.

CMJ — Concentric peak force.what: The highest force produced while driving up out of the jump.
CMJ — Concentric peak force.how: CMJ concentric peak force from ForceDecks (N).

CMJ — Eccentric impulse.what: How much braking force you build while dipping down before the jump.

CMJ — Take-off impulse.what: How much push you generate to leave the ground, relative to body weight.
CMJ — Take-off impulse.how: From the CMJ trials, as reported by ForceDecks.

SJ — P1 concentric impulse.what: The push in the first part of a squat jump, started from a still, bent-knee position.
SJ — P1 concentric impulse.how: Squat jump on ForceDecks (no dip before take-off); phase 1 concentric impulse.

SJ — P2 concentric impulse.what: The push in the final part of a squat jump, just before take-off.
SJ — P2 concentric impulse.how: Squat jump on ForceDecks; phase 2 concentric impulse.

SJ — Peak power.what: The most power produced in a squat jump from a still start, relative to body weight.

SLCMJ — Jump height (injured).what: How high you jump off the operated leg alone.
SLCMJ — Jump height (injured).how: Single-leg CMJ on ForceDecks, hands on hips; best of 3, injured side.

SLCMJ — Power/BW (injured).what: The power the operated leg produces in a single-leg jump.
SLCMJ — Power/BW (injured).how: Single-leg CMJ peak power, injured side, as reported by ForceDecks.

SL Drop Jump 15cm — RSI (injured).what: How springy the operated leg is: jump height compared with time on the ground after a small drop.
SL Drop Jump 15cm — RSI (injured).how: Single-leg drop jump from a 15 cm box on ForceDecks; best RSI, injured side.

SL Drop Jump 15cm — Jump height (injured.what: How high the operated leg rebounds after stepping off a 15 cm box.
SL Drop Jump 15cm — Jump height (injured.how: Single-leg drop jump from 15 cm; injured side.

SL Drop Jump 15cm — Ground contact time.what: How long the operated leg stays on the ground before rebounding. Shorter is better.
SL Drop Jump 15cm — Ground contact time.how: Single-leg drop jump from 15 cm; injured side (s).

Single hop LSI.what: How far you hop on the operated leg, as a percentage of the other leg.
Single hop LSI.how: Single hop for distance, best of 3 each leg; injured ÷ uninjured × 100.

Triple hop LSI.what: Distance covered in three hops on the operated leg, as a percentage of the other leg.
Triple hop LSI.how: Triple hop for distance, best of 3 each leg; injured ÷ uninjured × 100.

Crossover hop LSI.what: Distance covered in three zig-zag hops on the operated leg, as a percentage of the other leg.
Crossover hop LSI.how: Crossover hop for distance over a 15 cm strip; injured ÷ uninjured × 100.

6 m timed hop LSI.what: How quickly you hop 6 metres on the operated leg, compared with the other leg.
6 m timed hop LSI.how: 6 m timed hop; uninjured time ÷ injured time × 100.

Single-leg hop for distance (injured).what: How far you hop forward on the operated leg and land steadily.
Single-leg hop for distance (injured).how: Best of 3 with a controlled landing, injured side (cm).

Side hop (injured).what: How many side-to-side hops over a strip the operated leg can do in 30 seconds.
Side hop (injured).how: Side hop test: hops across two lines 40 cm apart in 30 s; count clean hops.

SEBT anterior reach composite (injured).what: How far you can reach forward with one foot while balancing on the operated leg.
SEBT anterior reach composite (injured).how: Star Excursion Balance Test, anterior reach as % of leg length.

split_squat.what: Single-leg strength in a split squat: the heaviest load you can lift 8 times on each leg.
split_squat.how: 8RM on each leg; enter the external load in kg.

sl_seated_calf_vald.what: Seated calf strength: how hard you can push up through the ball of one foot.
sl_seated_calf_vald.how: Seated single-leg isometric calf raise on VALD; peak force in N.

sl_seated_calf_smith.what: Seated calf strength: the heaviest load you can raise on one leg 8 times.
sl_seated_calf_smith.how: Smith machine, seated, knee at about 90°; 8RM in kg.

sl_knee_extension.what: Thigh (quadriceps) strength straightening one knee against a strength gauge.
sl_knee_extension.how: Isometric knee extension on the dynamometer; peak force in N.

sl_bridge.what: Hamstring and glute strength in a one-leg bridge: the heaviest load you can lift 8 times.
sl_bridge.how: 8RM single-leg bridge, knee at 30° flexion; load in kg.

sl_calf_raise_reps.what: Calf endurance: how many full heel raises you can do on one leg.
sl_calf_raise_reps.how: Body weight, full range, steady tempo; stop at fatigue or loss of form.

sl_calf_raise_loaded.what: Standing calf strength: the heaviest load you can raise on one leg 8 times.
sl_calf_raise_loaded.how: Standing single-leg calf raise with added load; 8RM in kg.

prone_hamstring_curl.what: Hamstring strength bending the knee while lying face down.
prone_hamstring_curl.how: Isometric prone knee flexion on the dynamometer; peak force in N.

hip_abduction.what: Outer-hip strength pushing your leg out to the side.
hip_abduction.how: Isometric hip abduction on the dynamometer; peak force in N.

hip_adduction.what: Inner-thigh (groin) strength squeezing your leg in towards the middle.
hip_adduction.how: Isometric hip adduction, same position as abduction; peak force in N.

hip_add_abd_ratio.what: The balance between groin and outer-hip strength on each leg.
hip_add_abd_ratio.how: Worked out by the app: adduction ÷ abduction.
